newsitem.title: IRAQ: Aziz says Iraq will not bow to U.S. pressure.
newsitem.headline: Aziz says Iraq will not bow to U.S. pressure.

text.p: Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz has said his country would not bow to the United Sates sabre-rattling and threats of use of force.

"Yes. We are much smaller than America which has a great power. But what shall we do? Shall we surrender? Definitely not because American greed knows no limit," Aziz told NTV-Moscow, a private Russian television station, in an interview in Baghdad on Thursday evening.

"They (Americans) are not satisfied with equal international relations...They want everything...They are leaving us no choice but to resist," Aziz said in the interview excerpts of which were made available to Reuters Television in Baghdad.
The full interview will be broadcast in Moscow on Sunday.
Aziz said the U.S. was violating Iraq's sovereignty and national security leaving his counry with no option but to fight back.
"What is happening is an aggression on us...aggression on our sovereignty and our national security. In a state like this we have no choice but to resist," he said.
The U.S. is massing warships in the Gulf and bombers in Kuwait to punish Iraq for defying no-fly zones over its territory.
The current crisis erupted when Iraqi President Saddam Hussein sent tank-equipped Republican Guards to help a pro- Baghdad Kurdish rebel leader rout rivals in northern Iraq.
Massoud Barzani and his Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), who aligned themselves with Baghdad recently, are in control of most of Iraq's Kurdish north.
Aziz said Iraq was aware of the risks involved in the military standoff with the U.S. and urged world public opinion "to exercise pressure on America to stop its aggression on Iraq".

Aziz, in a statement to the official Iraqi News Agency on Thursday, also warned Kuwait against allowing U.S. Stealth bombers to use its territory for possible bombing raids on Iraq, saying the decision was tantamount to an act of war.
But he softened his stand in an interview with CNN later, excerpts of which were carried by the official press on Friday.

"My statement did not include a threat to Kuwait. We did not threaten Kuwait. We wanted its people to be acquainted with the aggressive decision of their rulers," the papers quoted Aziz as telling CNN.
The ruling Baath party newspaper al-Thawra, in a fiery anti- U.S. editorial, urged President Bill Clinton on Friday to educate Americans on how to open dialogue with countries they are at odds with.
Denouncing Clinton as criminal, the paper said:

"The civilised behaviour, which American politicians do not know and do not seem to practise requires...a civilised method represented in dialogue and the educating of the American people on the principles of human relations with other peoples and the pursuit of correct diplomacy in solving problems."
